London Now. “Imagine this reader, at the click of a button, every public library in the UK is lost, destroyed, forgotten. Would you even notice this change? Well according to the Arts Council England, only 30% of the general public (aged over 16) have used public libraries in the last year. To put this in perspective, in 2006, roughly half of the adult population in the UK had used public libraries that year. This drastic decline has been often attributed to the increasing use of modern technology such as Mobile phones and ebooks, leading to less people actually needing to use a physical book. Does this mean that modern public libraries are obsolete?” … “change is inevitable and thus libraries no longer have the purpose of holding information, but rather now have a duty of providing a safe space for people to hang out, to have fun and to read.”

entity: Why the Long Wait for Your Library E
text: Book? – Santa Barbara Independent. “An individual consumer pays about $13 on average for an e-book and receives ongoing access. A public library typically pays $55 or more for a license that may last only two years and allow only one reader at a time to borrow the book. When the license expires, the library may have to pay again to continue providing the same title. This challenge is being felt here at home. At the Santa Barbara Public Library, digital materials are provided through several different licensing models, many of which expire after two years.”

Americans are losing faith in shared institutions, but public libraries are one of the few we still trust – Hechinger Report. ” it’s important to point out that while visits to libraries have not yet rebounded to pre-pandemic levels, they are growing, in part because their program offerings are expanding. Adults and children in the U.S. made more than 800 million visits to a library in 2023, an average of 2.2 million visits per day and nearly double the number in 2021. There are over 17,000 public library locations in the United States — more than the number of hospitals or McDonald’s.” Microsoft and US public libraries launch AI literacy initiative – Digwatch. “Microsoft has announced a partnership with the Public Library Association (PLA), a division of the American Library Association, to expand access to free artificial intelligence (AI) literacy training across the USA. A new book revisits the years when Bombay’s working-class libraries were flourishing – Scroll. “As Bombay expanded in the late 19th century and early 20th century, it developed a strong library culture, which came to be organised along various lines – religious communities, neighbourhoods, and secular educational institutions. On the one hand, there were community-led libraries, such as the Mulla Firoz Library (established in 1830), containing books relating to Zoroastrian religion, the Jain Reading Room and Library, the Jamestji Nasarwanji Petit Fore Reading Room and Library by Parsis, the MJ Khoja Library and the Anjuman-i-Islam by Muslims. On the other hand, there were strong neighbourhood libraries, such as the Native General Library (established in 1845) in Dhobi Talao and Sr D Petit Khanda Mohalla Library in Nizampura.”

Library Adventures includes craft sessions, author visits, inclusive family activities, and monthly Active Saturdays led by leisure centre staff.”

entity: Judith’s a library loyalty card winner
text: Around Wellington. “Following the introduction of a loyalty card scheme at Wellington Library, the October prize draw winner has been announced. Local resident Judith chose a £30 voucher donated by the Cheese and Wine Shop in South Street. The loyalty card scheme has been introduced by Somerset Libraries as part of National Year of Reading 2026 and Wellington’s Cradle to Career – Reading Town project.”

Free blood pressure checks available at Shrewsbury Library – Shropshire Star. “Free blood pressure checks available at a Shropshire library are being backed by a town MP as a quick and simple way of identifying health problems.” Ludlow Library to host free Green Libraries Week events – Ludlow Advertiser.

Ainsdale Library and Hesketh Park Conservatory among landmarks which community groups could run – Stand Up for Southport. The now closed Ainsdale Library is now available for any community group to run as they wish. ““This policy means community organisations, charities and social enterprises can take on the management of Council-owned buildings and facilities for operation in ways that will deliver long-term benefits for local people.”

Wednesbury library temporarily closed after asbestos was discovered – Express and Star. “Wednesbury Library in Walsall Street, Wednesbury, will be closing from October 5 while urgent building work to remove the material. The library will be closed for most of next month for specialist contractors to remove the asbestos. It is scheduled to reopen on October 26.” Sandwell Libraries secures almost £100,000 to launch creative festival across three towns – Sandwell Council. “Sandwell Libraries secured £99,908 from Arts Council England through National Lottery Project Grants for a new programme of cultural activity. Making It in Sandwell is a 10-month creativity festival celebrating the borough’s rich industrial heritage and vibrant creative talent. Beginning this October, the programme will bring a wide range of cultural activities into libraries across the three towns, helping more people access arts and culture within their local communities.”

Commemorative Dolly Parton plaque set for Paisley Central Library – The National. Erskine Library to reopen in temporary home on 9th November – Renfrewshire 24. “Erskine Library is expected to reopen in its new temporary home in the grounds of Erskine Sports Centre on 9th November. The library will close temporarily to the public from 24th October to allow the move from its current home in Bridgewater Shopping Centre.”
Successful summer of reading in Reading – Reading Council. 1300 children and 25 volunteers. “Almost 300 teens and adults also enjoyed the Reading loves reading challenge by joining in Book Bingo.”
Plymouth libraries extend hours and strengthen community links – Exmouth Journal.

Date confirmed for Central Library’s move from Broadway to Northminster as part of £6m revamp – Peterborough Telegraph. “The library will close on Friday 30 October to allow for all the books and other services to be transferred to a temporary library in Northminster House in Northminster Road, Peterborough, and will be known as Northminster Library.” … “The refurbishment of Central Library is being designed to meet the changing needs of the community, with dedicated areas for community groups, events and other activities. The project is funded by the city council’s Regeneration Fund including monies from the Government’s Towns Fund.”

Library is ‘bridging cultures and building friendships’ – BBC. “In October 2025, Kennington in Oxfordshire officially twinned with Musanda in western Kenya – the heart of Abingdon-based charity The Nasio Trust’s community work. In 2024, Oxford author Sylvia Vetta jointly lead a project with the charity to deliver Cosmic Cats – an anthology of stories by Kennington and Kenyan students, aiming to raise funds for the facility.” Banking Hub opens at the library – Henley Herald. Henley Library. “Both personal and businesses banking transactions can be accessed at the counter including cash and cheque deposits, cash withdrawals, change for businesses and balance queries. Each day there is a different bank representative available for private consultations. No booking is required. Monday is Barclays, Tuesday HSBC, Wednesday Lloyds/Halifax/Bank of Scotland and Thursday Nat West.” … “A permanent site for the Banking Hub is hoped to be found on the high street by July 2027 with an outside ATM.”

Oldham Library to host football-inspired fairy tale show – Oldham Times. “Footy Fairy Tales, created by North West-based theatre company Yarnbird Arts, is aimed at children aged five to 11 and asks: “What happens when football and fairy tales collide?”” Royton Library finds a new temporary home as essential repair works progress – Oldham Council. “The library will reopen at a temporary location from Monday 19 October, ensuring residents can continue to access book lending services in their community.” … “The move follows the temporary closure of Royton Library on Rochdale Road to allow investigations and repairs to flooring within the building. The works are essential to ensure library remains a safe, welcoming and accessible space for the future.”

The Queen of Crime is coming to Inspire and Nottingham City libraries for Agatha Christie: A World of Mystery exhibition and events programme this autumn – Marketing Nottingham. “As a member of the Living Knowledge Network, Inspire has partnered with Nottingham City Libraries to host a free taster of the exhibition opening at the British Library on 30 October” … “Can you crack the case? Readers are invited to take part in the Crime Reading Challenge, running between 30 October 2026 and 31 July 2027. The challenge encourages participants to read their way through a selection of great crime novels, gathering clues and following the trail to uncover whodunnit. Children can also put their detective skills to the test and take part in a special Clue Hunt Activity at selected libraries this October half term”

Local author runs free children’s session at Berwick Library for the Berwick Literary Festival – Northumberland Gazette. “Carolina Knight Ewing, the author of Felix and Everly’s Mini Adventures, will be running a free session in Berwick Library for early readers (suitable for 5-10 years old with accompanying parent) with tickets available from The Maltings website as part of the Berwick Literary Festival.”
The Firework-Maker’s Daughter touring North Yorkshire – Northern Echo. Free “Performances will be held at libraries in Selby, Tadcaster, Ripon, Northallerton, Scarborough and Pickering.”

Roadshows bring health and wellbeing support to local communities – North Somerset Council. “Free health and wellbeing roadshows are coming to Weston and Portishead libraries later this month, providing an opportunity to access advice, support and information from a range of local services in one place.”

Library roadshows seek views on adult disability support – North Northamptonshire Council. “People are invited to series of roadshows inviting people to help design and develop groups and activities for adults with disabilities in North Northamptonshire.” Free digital support sessions available during Get Online Week at North Northamptonshire Council libraries – North Northamptonshire Council.

Lyons: Public Libraries Consultation launched – Department for Communities NI. “This consultation provides an opportunity for everyone to help shape how my Department and Libraries NI will support and develop our public libraries through the opportunities and challenges of the next ten years. I encourage everyone to take part and share their views.” The public consultation is open now and runs until 25 November 2026 Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough Council joins local groups to celebrate Good Relations Week 2026 – Antrim and Newtownabbey Council. Several events in libraries “The programme ranges from workshops, exhibitions and film screenings to theatre, music, storytelling, sport and panel discussions. The events will give people opportunities to meet, share experiences and hear perspectives different from their own.”

Zine Making with Norwich Millennium Zine Library – Visit Norwich. “Norwich Millennium Zine Library is on the first floor of the Norfolk & Norwich Millennium Library and has 200+ zines on topics like activism, protest, local interest, gender, sexuality, photography, art, nature, and more. Any zines you make in this session can be donated to the Zine Library collection! All materials will be provided.” Carnegie Clock set to return to Gorleston after restoration – Eastern Daily Press. “The Carnegie Clock is set to be installed opposite Gorleston Library, in front of The Feathers pub, decades after it was removed from its original site during the demolition of the old library more than 50 years ago.”

STEM Starts launches programme to inspire digital confidence in young people – Moray Council. “As part of the wider Code Xtra initiative, the programme will contribute to the establishment of community coding and AI hubs across Scotland”
Blooming brilliant Green Libraries Week returns – Monmouthshire Council. Events.

Midlothian libraries offer free cost of living support this autumn and winter – Midlothian View. “Midlothian Council is highlighting the wide range of services available through its libraries, which are free to use and open to everyone.”

Library closed after rent row could become bookies – BBC. “Breck Road Library, in the Anfield area of Liverpool, has been closed since November 2025 after a rent dispute. Ruth Knox, from Save Liverpool Libraries, said turning three quarters of the Mall site into a betting shop would offer little to the community and there was already a “surplus” of bookies in the area. She said the library was a haven for all sorts of people – from mums and toddlers who attended baby groups to children accessing books for school projects to jobseekers. The BBC has contacted BoyleSports (UK) Ltd, which is planning to convert the site, for comment.” ‘Books not Bookies’ as campaigners urge planners to keep Anfield library open – Birkenhead News. “Since the library shut, campaigners have used their weekends to set up outside the building – across from which you can see another bookmakers’ site – lobbying for support to urge Liverpool Council to reopen the library. After a sudden downpour, Ruth Knox and Sue Ferguson from the Save Liverpool Libraries campaign set up their table outside with petitions calling for the planning application to be rejected. Sitting in front of a sign reading “Books Not Bookies”, Ruth said, “We’ve been here so long, people have got to know us.” Sue added, “This is an essential service.”

Lewisham town centre update: Costs up to £30.5 million and library operator chosen – From the Murky Depths.”As for the library, the latest council report highlights “the award of the Lewisham Library Operator concession contract to Blue Garage Ltd for a period of five years with the option to extend for up to a further 5 years at a value of £10,704,000 over the full contract period.””
Free talks, workshops and activities on offer during Green Libraries Week – Leicester Council. List of events, including with authors.

Find out more about Lancaster library building work at drop-in event – Lancaster Guardian. Rawtenstall Library restoration project to continue into early 2027 – Lancashire Council. “Work to the roof and upper floors of the Grade II listed Carnegie building is almost complete and has progressed largely as planned, helping to protect the long-term future of the historic library.”
in-Law’s Dresses: Black History Month celebration returns to Brixton Library – Saturday 10th October – Brixton Buzz.
the Carnegie Library occupation, ten years on – Brixton Buzz.

tensions rise in Myatt’s Fields ahead of Thursday’s by-election – 8th October 2026 – Brixton Buzz. “Labour is accusing the Greens of planning cuts to Minet Library. But the £498,000 library savings target at the centre of the row was carried over from Labour’s own budget.”

Public statement: complaint – Lambeth Council. “The videos use statements made by a council officer to support the allegation that the council’s previous administration agreed a savings proposal in the March budget to reduce library hours and library services. This is not correct.” Hundreds demand Lambeth protect Head of Libraries post as restructure threatens role – Brixton Buzz. “Hundreds of library users, professionals, authors and community groups have signed an open letter (see end of article) calling on Lambeth Council to reverse plans to delete the post of Head of Service for Lambeth Libraries and Archives.” … “Susanna Barnes, who has led the service through years of cuts, closures and the fight to save Carnegie Library, is set to lose her role under a restructure that would merge Libraries, Archives, Leisure Centres and Culture into a single post at a lower grade. The only role ringfenced for the new position is the current Service Manager for leisure …”

Huyton Library consultation results – Knowsley News. “Over 200 people have shared their views on Huyton Library as part of an in-person and online consultation which ran from 17 August to 14 September 2026. The feedback will inform the development of the new Huyton Hive building on Cavendish Walk. Huyton Hive, located in the former B&M unit in the heart of the village centre, is being transformed into a vibrant, modern library on the ground floor with Knowsley Works (providing employment and training support to residents) and office space being created on the first floor.”

Huddersfield’s New Library Hub Officially Opened As Part of Our Cultural Heart Development – Kirklees Local TV. “Huddersfield’s new library hub has officially opened its doors today (21 September), marking the completion of the first major phase of the town’s £200 million Our Cultural Heart regeneration scheme” … Councillor “described the new library as “a new start for Kirklees”, adding that the opening of Queensgate Square would provide another opportunity for residents to see the changes taking place in the town centre.” … “The new children’s library has been a particular focus, with families exploring the space on opening day.” … “Arts Council England funding will support a programme of events running until next April, including textiles, theatre and appearances from authors and poets. A new Library Adventures trail will also encourage families to explore different areas of the building.” New Huddersfield Library Hub footage shows hard work behind the scenes – Yorkshire Live. “It also shines a light on the role of the Yorkshire Purchasing Organisation in the creation of the new facility” … “The organisation also supported the design of the enchanted forest-themes children’s area, with its appointed supplier, FG Library, taking the lead.”

Petition to save once thriving Tunbridge Wells community centre now ‘underused’ and where library has ‘poorest attendance in Kent’ – Kent Live. “library hours slashed from 28 to 15″ in 2015. ” the local councillor at the time said that the first volunteers at TN2 were sadly too old to be involved, had moved away, or had even died, and that it had been impossible to find new ones.” … “no decision had been taken to close the centre, which it said was occupied by a number of users, including the library.” Residents asked for views on new library plans – BBC. “The current Shepway library building is due to be demolished and the service will move to Shepway youth and community centre as its long-term home, Kent County Council (KCC) said. It will provide access to books, learning, activities and digital equipment, while creating opportunities for library, youth and community teams to work together, the council said. A six-week consultation has started to gather views on the design, facilities and activities that should be included in the new space.”
Netflix inspired shelf to appear in Jersey Library – Bailiwick Express. “A total of 20 books will line a shelf with accompanying signage.”

Protesters fight possible cuts to library service – Islington Tribune. “The Tribune reported last month that the Town Hall had spent tens of thousands on a consultancy group to deliver a review on the borough’s library service. Union staff say they were then told by senior council officers that this could amount to cuts of £500,000 to £1million.” Jeremy Corbyn and Michael Rosen join protests over fears Islington library funding could be cut by £1m – NW Londoner. “Statements from the pair were read at a public demonstration on Thursday 24 September, where campaigners called for Islington Council to abandon its review of services. They described public libraries as a “foundation of our community” and “a safe and welcoming environment for thousands of people in our community.””

£80,000-Plus Library Cuts Put On Hold By Isle Of Wight Councillors – Isle of Wight Radio. “The council’s economy, regeneration, transport and infrastructure committee voted on Tuesday (October 6) to hold further discussions with partners rather than send the proposals to the next stage of the budget process. The suggested savings include changing how partnership libraries operate, potentially transferring more responsibility to town and parish councils, and reducing opening days at some council-run libraries.” Isle Of Wight Libraries Announce Spooktacular Half-Term Activities – Isle of Wight Radio.

Free musical instrument library to launch in Greenock – Greenock Telegraph. “The service is being supported by We Make Music Scotland and the Youth Music Initiative” Greenock library has spaces on weekly history course – Greenock Telegraph. “informal, tutor-led course “

Next chapter for library as group handed control – BBC. “Volunteers took over the running of Anlaby Park Community Library when it was due to shut in 2013 due to budget cuts by the council. The authority has now approved the library for a 35-year Community Asset Transfer (CAT) to “ensure its long-term viability as a community-focused hub”.”

Giving every baby a strong start with library membership from birth – Hounslow Council. “Hounslow Council is helping every child begin their love of books from day one by introducing My First Library Card for babies, at birth. Under the new initiative, families will receive their child’s first Hounslow library card when they register their baby’s birth, alongside their Bookstart pack.”

‘The greatest pleasure is the people’ – Life on the road as the far north’s mobile library driver – Northern Times. “, behind the wheel of High Life Highland’s Brora mobile library, he travels through Sutherland and Caithness, enjoying the landscape and getting to know the people who depend on its visits.”

entity: Hemel Hempstead library to open later after Sunday closure plan scrapped
text: Hemel Today. “Controversial plans to end Sunday openings at Hemel Hempstead, as well as Bishop’s Stortford, St Albans, Stevenage, Watford and Welwyn Garden City libraries were put forward earlier this year, in a bid to cut costs by £129,000.”
Official Opening of Huddersfield Library Hub

Hertfordshire County Council set to cut library hours – Watford Observer. “Plans to cut opening hours at Watford Central Library and five others in Hertfordshire have been unveiled just weeks after plans to shut them on Sundays were shelved … Ending Sunday openings in Watford, Hemel Hempstead, St Albans, Stevenage, Welwyn Garden City, and Bishop’s Stortford was planned in a bid to cut costs by £129,000 before protests forced a U-turn. However, it left officials scrambling to find alternative hours reductions” … “The revised hours – which are due to take effect from January 1 – will be presented to members of the council’s resources and performance cabinet panel on Wednesday (October 7).”

Stronger Hereford Fund backs away from Shirehall library project – Hereford Times. “The Stronger Hereford Board, set up six years ago to bid for and administer a large pot of Government money intended for 15 separate projects in the city, says it is recommending that its further contribution to the project to create a new library and learning centre in the grade II* neo-Classical building should not proceed. In a downbeat update in August, Herefordshire Council, which owns the building, confirmed it was still expecting that £2.6 million from the Stronger Towns Fund would fund a new library within the early 19th century building, though with a less costly layout in mind”

Harold Wood Library building to reopen as community-led vision becomes reality – Havering Council. “The building, which closed in March 2025, will now return to public use through a community-led model developed by the Harold Wood Foundation. The partnership will see the building transformed into a vibrant centre for learning, community activity, wellbeing and support services for local residents.”
Shining a light on “hidden disability” – Hartlepool Council. Talks at two libraries on Developmental Language Disorder.

Basingstoke library work almost complete as staff move in – Basingstoke Gazette.”Hampshire County Council is carrying out a restructure of the town centre library -Basingstoke Discovery Centre – after deciding to reduce the size of it by almost a quarter. The plans will see the Festival Place library space reduce from 1,300sqm to 1,000sqm.” North Baddesley library gets grant for signs and books – Hampshire Chronicle. Volunteer-run. Received funding from local Test Valley Borough Councillors.

Focus on reading’s benefits for mental health – BBC. “Guille-Alles Library and Guernsey Mind have formed a partnership to mark World Mental Health Day and encourage islanders to discover the “positive impact” reading can have. As part of the day, a collection of books have been displayed at the library featuring subjects recommended by Guernsey Mind to help people relax and learn.”

Stroud welcomes new free community library The Open Book – Stroud News and Journal. “The Open Book has opened at 57 London Road, Stroud, next to the former Stroud Town Council offices, offering a library, reading room and meeting space. The collection has largely been created from retired academic Richard House’s private library, built up over around 50 years.” … “Unlike a traditional library, visitors cannot borrow books to take home. Instead, The Open Book provides a space where people can browse and read the collection, carry out research or discuss books with other visitors.” Stroud Library launches new mood-boosting book collection – Stroud News and Journal. “Stroud Library welcomed readers and partners on Saturday, October 10, for the launch of Mood-Boosting Books 2026, a collection of ten titles chosen by young adults to support everyday wellbeing. More than 100 book recommendations were submitted by young adults aged 18 to 25 from across the country.”
Agatha Christie exhibition coming to Mitchell Library – Glasgow Times.

First look at new plans for Falkirk’s new Town Hall – Falkirk Council. “The public drop-in event is designed to gather the views of residents before a planning application is submitted. The event will be held on the second floor of Falkirk Library on Tuesday 27 October, from 3pm to 8pm.” … “The plans bring together a range of civic, cultural and community functions within a single building, including a theatre, studio theatre, public library, public studios, council chamber, council workspaces, advice and support services, and café facilities.”
Typewriter art exhibition honours literary legends – BBC. Colchester Library.

Plans to convert former library into nursery submitted – Enfield Dispatch. “Little Learners Nurseries Ltd is applying to Enfield Council to repurpose Winchmore Hill Library into a “day nursery and early years childcare facility” …”Winchmore Hill was one of seven libraries closed by the former Labour administration at Enfield Civic Centre in July 2025 – understood to be the highest number of libraries closed at any one time by a London borough council.”
People power needed to steer active travel in East Dunbartonshire – East Dunbartonshire Council. Drop-ins in libraries for consultation.

Dumfries libraries host green events and Halloween swaps – Deadline News. Green Libraries Week events plus “Alongside the programme, the council’s Scare, Share and Wear initiative encourages families to reuse Halloween costumes rather than throw them away.”
Libraries launch Halloween costume scheme – Mid Devon Advertiser.
Neurodivergent group at Halesowen Library

lipped on possible job losses – Mid-Devon Advertiser. “Libraries Unlimited confirmed an internal staff consultation had begun, and that while it was ongoing, it could not elaborate on it.” … cuts “could see the number of so-called library supervisors reduced. The move by Libraries Unlimited comes just months after the county’s library service looked secure when Devon County Council opted not to instigate potential changes that could have altered opening hours and grouped libraries together in hubs.”

Exeter Library row erupts again as councillors trade claims over safeguarding – Exmouth Journal. QueerFest: “A bitter safeguarding dispute has spilled into a heated email row between county councillors, with accusations of spreading hate speech, dismissing legitimate concerns and making light of a serious subject. The exchange follows continuing controversy surrounding an event held at Exeter Library last year and questions over how safeguarding concerns raised afterwards were handled.” … “councillors had previously received complaints about the event and raised questions about age guidance, safeguarding assessments and how decisions about material and activities had been made.” see also County councillor punished for raising safeguarding concerns after sex toys were displayed at LGBTQIA+ event near children’s area at Exeter Library – Free Speech Union and Reform UK councillor sues Lib Dem authority over library stall promoting ‘chemsex’ – GB News. Communities invited to apply for new Devon library improvement grants – Devon Council. “The grants are available through the new Re-imagined Library Spaces Fund and Enhanced Library Offers Fund, which together provide £300,000 of investment for projects that improve access, strengthen community connections and create new opportunities for people to use and benefit from their local library. The first funding opportunities will open on Thursday 1 October 2026.”

New ice cream van-style mobile libraries hit road – BBC. “”One little boy thinking I was an ice cream van, when he saw the books he was overjoyed.” A new chapter has begun for Derbyshire’s mobile library service with two new vans heading out across the county. The Peugeot Boxer vans have replaced two lorries which Derbyshire County Council said were in “poor condition” and regularly out of action awaiting repairs.”

Library closes for a week to install new lights – BBC. “Workington Library will be temporarily shut until Monday 12 October while work is done on the ground floor of the building.” Carlisle Library Transformation Marked with Official Opening Celebration – Cumberland Council. “Cumberland Council has officially celebrated the transformation of Carlisle Library with an opening ceremony, following the library’s successful public reopening in August. Guests were invited to explore the transformed building and experience the wide range of services now available. The evening included guided tours, demonstrations of digital archive services, showcases of children’s and family activities, presentations from Adult Learning, and opportunities to discover more about the renowned Jackson Collection, which now has a permanent home within the library.”
‘Dilapidated’ phone box transformed into library – BBC.

Northwich Library welcomed a very special visitor this week – Silk Radio. “Sir Hugo Brunner, the great grandson of Sir John Tomlinson Brunner, was given a tour around the library building, which is currently being renovated ahead of reopening in 2027. Sir Hugo’s father, Sir Felix Brunner, opened the extension to the current library in 1951 and his great grandfather, Sir John Tomlinson Brunner, commissioned the construction of the original Northwich Library building.”

Victoria Coren Mitchell to launch Belsize Library’s 90th birthday – Ham and High. “A launch evening will take place at the Antrim Road venue on Thursday, October 15 with live music, refreshments, and speakers including Coren Mitchell, Tulip Siddiq MP, Rashid Iqbal of The Winch, and Anthony Isaacs of Friends of the Library.” … “Camden Council ran the building until 2012 and is still the owner, but after threatening to close it altogether local youth and family charity The Winchester Project stepped in to manage it as a library and community space.”

‘Community spirit survives’: The 100-year-old Halifax library rescued by volunteers which is now busier than ever – Halifax Courier. Council passed Skircoat Green Library to volunteers in 2020. “Taking in around £20,000 a year, the addition of a cafe has provided a key income stream for the library, which also relies on donations and grants. It hosts talks and children’s events, and has a host of regular borrowers who visit at least once a week. The fact that it is open on a Sunday is particularly welcomed by many.”

Radcliffe Library to temporarily close ahead of move to new £40m Hub – My News Desk. “Radcliffe Library at Stand Lane will temporarily close at 1.00pm on Saturday 3 October 2026 as preparations begin to move services into their new home at The Hub. The temporary closure will allow library staff to relocate stock, equipment and services to Radcliffe’s new £40 million Hub building, which will bring together library, leisure and wellbeing services in a modern, purpose-built town centre facility.”

The Rat Catcher: one performance down, don’t miss out – Buckinghamshire Council. “With its cosy crime feel and nods to the Golden Age of mystery, The Rat Catcher puts the audience right at the heart of the story.” High Wycombe Library Gardens restoration planned after drought damage- Bucks Free Press. “follows criticism of the green space, which was described in a historical account as a “shadow of their former self”, compared with the floral displays of previous decades.”
Carnegie Library Hub look for new members to join their team – Brixton Buzz. Interestingly wide range of volunteer posts listed.

Libraries to open for longer and abolish overdue fines to get more Bristolians reading – Bristol Post. Council ” consulted the public about libraries, and found widespread desire for them to open longer, including in evenings and weekends. The draft library strategy is due to be approved by the public health and communities policy committee on Monday, October 19.” No increase in budget so “One option is asking librarians to spread out across different branches, supported by volunteers. So instead of having two members of staff working in smaller libraries, there could be just one member of staff instead, but always accompanied by a volunteer. ” see also Libraries could rely on unpaid work to extend opening hours – B24/7.

entity: Bridgend – Awen invests in Ukrainian, Polish and children’s Braille books
text: Awen Cultural Trust (press release). “Thanks to a Libraries as Sanctuaries grant from Welsh Government, Awen Cultural Trust has invested in new Ukrainian, Polish and children’s Braille books, helping more children and families access stories in the language and format that best meets their need”. £2450 invested.

Bradford children’s book schemes join Dolly Parton-inspired day of giving – Telegraph and Argus. “Imagination Library schemes across the Bradford district are marking the first-ever Give Like Dolly Day, which takes place on September 25 in honour of Dolly Parton and her lifelong commitment to giving every child the gift of reading.” … “Keighley’s Imagination Library scheme was paused earlier this year due to funding shortages.”

three ditches dug at Upton Library – Dorset Echo. “ditches were dug by bikes and e-bikes at Upton Library, damaging flowerbeds and creating trip hazards, the council said. The incident took place at the library on September 2 and a member of its Outside Operations team had to refill the holes after tending the beds and borders the previous day.”

Three week delay in reopening library after seagulls discovered nesting in roof – Bournemouth Echo. “Poole Library has been closed since August 26 as work is underway to remove reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC) from the roof.” Expected reopen October 19. Asbestos removed from Charminster Library roof as repairs continue – Bournemouth Echo. “Charminster Library has been closed since December 2025 after a partial ceiling collapse.” … ““We remain committed to exploring ways of reopening this important community asset, and we will keep our residents up”dated.

Council wins prestigious sustainability award – Birmingham Council. “The award also highlighted the council’s commitment to promoting high energy standards in public buildings, including the Library of Birmingham. Achieving a BREEAM Excellent rating, the library has prioritised energy efficiency throughout its operation, supporting the conservation of nationally important archive collections such as Shakespeare’s First Folio. Although now 13 years old, the Library of Birmingham has recently been recognised by government surveyors as a UK exemplar in efficient energy use among public buildings. How one community’s love kept historic baths alive – BBC. “Work on the Grade II*-listed building in Birmingham’s Balsall Heath has been underway since 2023, as part of a £32.7m restoration of the swimming pool and neighbouring Balsall Heath library.” … “As part of the renovation, the two buildings will be connected and a mezzanine floor will be built into the library to meet the needs of the community.” Library set to open Summer 2027

Rosneath’s library reopens – Lochside Press. “Rosneath’s library officially reopened today, redecorated and with extra shelves for books and DVDs, as well as a comfy seating area for adults. The village library was never reopened by LiveArgyll after the first lockdown in March 2020 but now it has been taken on by the community group Rosneath Proud.”

Da Nang Library undergoes digital transformation and develops knowledge resources – Vietnam VN. “During the period 2020-2025, 100% of commune and ward libraries will be connected to the Internet, use the integrated electronic library management software Ilibweb, and be equipped with equipment to support professional activities such as computers, printers, and barcode scanners.”

Platteville library to offer free shredding services – Telegraph Herald. “Members of the public are invited to bring a total of up to two grocery bags or one bankers box of papers per person for destruction to the library”

Amid turmoil, SLC library board launches investigation into management, alleged retaliation – Salt Lake Tribune. “Another former employee, Diana Castro, said a library executive accused her of sowing division through a workplace wellness committee that she ran. “I was accused of bullying, sabotage and disengagement without a single opportunity to review the claims beforehand or prepare a response,” she said. “I felt belittled, misrepresented and completely abandoned. The workplace to which I had dedicated nearly a decade of my life, the library I loved so dearly, was no longer a place where I felt safe.””

Texan public libraries generate nearly $5 for every public dollar invested, study finds – Dallas News. “Texas public libraries generated $4.74 in community value for every $1 invested in fiscal year 2024, according to a state-wide study released Wednesday.” … “The report estimates that libraries produced $3.8 billion in total economic benefits and supported 11,200 jobs across the state.” … “The findings come as several libraries across the state are weighing reductions in library staffing. Dallas’ proposed budget eliminates 72 library positions while keeping all 29 branches open. San Antonio’s proposed budget cuts includes 39 library positions, although city officials say affected employees could be reassigned rather than laid off.” Next Episode – Texas State Libraries. “… the Small Library Management Training Program is entering its next chapter. The newest iteration of SLM shifts its focus toward developing management competencies that support responsive, effective library leadership. Rather than concentrating on frontline library service skills, the program emphasizes the knowledge and practices needed to guide organizations through growth and change.”
Millvale Community Library breaks ground on dedicated space for tool lending program – WPXI-TV

Library board overrules staff, removes sexually explicit books from teen section – Christian Post. “A staff committee recommended moving a fifth book, People Kill People by Ellen Hopkins, from the teen section to the adult section, and the board unanimously upheld the recommendation.”

Oregon library book challenges rise 20% with focus on protected groups – Statesman Journal. “While most challenges were to materials, 22% focused on library programs, displays, or services and included a challenge to all adult graphic novels, objections to Banned Books Week and Pride Month displays, and a claim that the Dolly Parton Imagination Library “indoctrinates” children to Christianity, according to the report.” In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement – Architectural Record. “Its architecture evokes the region’s forests without lapsing into rusticity: a board-formed concrete base supports massive timber columns and fluted ultra-high-performance concrete panels, while the roof stretches 55 feet, like a front-porch awning, to cover the two entrances.”

Clydebank residents encouraged to use mobile library – Clydebank Post. “Councillor Lauren Oxley is reminding people about the valuable service, which will return to the streets this week after a brief break for maintenance work.”

Support your wellbeing and your community through helping others – Council. Volunteering. The Discovery Den: Sensory Mobile Library – Council. “The Discovery Den: Sensory Mobile Library will be the UK’s first mobile sensory public library. A fully equipped, accessible, environmentally friendly, electric vehicle housing a small interactive sensory space for children and young people with special educational needs and/or disabilities. Expected to be in operation from early 2026, the vehicle will visit a selection of schools and community locations across Warwickshire offering sensory space for small group use, a custom book selection and sensory equipment for loan.”

Chislehurst Library reopens after major refurbishment – This is Local London. “Chislehurst Library will reopen following the completion of refurbishment work as the fifth library to re-open as part of the £11m initiative to modernise libraries across the borough. Executive Councillor for Renewal, Recreation and Housing, Yvonne Bear, said: “This is literally an investment in our future which also minimises maintenance costs going forward.”

Work to transform Sale Library set to begin soon – About Manchester. “Work to transform Sale Library into a state-of-the-art facility is set to begin soon.The library and foyer area on the ground floor of Sale Waterside will be given a fabulous fresh new look and exciting new features – including a permanent exhibition space for the Cosgrove Hall Films Archive. Residents were able to share their thoughts at our public consultation event in June and feedback has played a key role in shaping the final design and décor of the new space.”
Chichester’s Pesky Rat hits the road on libraries tour – Sussex Express.

Best selling author and creator of Vera to visit Southwold – EADT. Ann Cleeves. Pantomime dame hits out at council’s ‘attack’ after library storytime events cancelled – Independent. “Mama G, who is an LGBTQ+ campaigner and a former Britain’s Got Talent contestant, said she was devastated when she received the news her performances in Suffolk libraries this summer have been postponed after seven years of storytelling there.”

South Ayrshire Council awarded Green Libraries Grant – Ayrshire Today. CILIPS Scotland grant “The council’s Libraries, Art and Culture service will use the £2,000 fund to create a sustainable living and literacy programme, dubbed ‘One Small Thing’.”

Library launches new Orkney Flora Trail – Council. “Orkney Library and Archive’s Interactive Orcadian Flora Trail explores local wildflowers and habitats, through planters, poetry recordings in local dialect, and more. A series of raised planters describes a range of habitats – coastal, meadow, woodland, moorland, roadside – and the specific types of wildflowers typically found there. The wheelchair-friendly planters were made by staff and service users at the Council’s St Colms facility which works with folks with learning disabilities to develop employability and skills development opportunities.”

Weston-super-Mare MP launches campaign to save Worle Library – Weston Mercury. “North Somerset Council looks to cut library spending by a fifth. Mr Aldridge MP said it is vital that Worle does not become the next community to lose its library. Worle Library was visited 22,000 times in 2024/25. However, following the discovery of wet rot and damp in February the council said it cannot afford the significant costs required to repair and maintain the building. “
North Lincolnshire Council champions Summer Reading Challenge – Council. Story Garden. “over 900 children participating by early August”

What next for Newham’s libraries – Council. “Residents are being asked to share their views through a ten-part questionnaire, available online or in libraries, on how they want the service to develop in the future.”

entity: Moray – Proposed cuts to Keith Library hours see users sign protest petition
text: Grampian Online. “Townsfolk are signing a petition against moves to slash Keith Library’s opening hours. Upset residents are now urging others to add their names to the document before it’s handed over to Moray Council.”
Leeds libraries overhaul IT systems to cut login times and save £65k a year – Yorkshire Evening Post. Computers to run Chrome.

Haringey Council consultation on future of its 9 libraries – Ham and High. “The council is encouraging residents to complete online surveys to help develop its new library service strategy, saying it wants to know “what you like about your libraries, how you think they can improve, and what is currently missing from them” … “Among the comments on the library user survey submitted so far, residents mentioned the delayed reopening of Muswell Hill Library, which has been closed for two and a half years, the need for longer opening hours, especially in the evenings, and wanting more events.”
Glasgow Life poised to appoint Director for Libraries, Sport and Community Engagement – Herald Scotland. Vacancy for post paying £102,894 and £116,854 and a deadline of 28 September 2025.

Clacton Library redevelopment gets the green light – Tendry District Council. “Planning permission has been granted for the redevelopment of Clacton Library, paving the way for the creation of a new, multi-purpose community space. The redevelopment will bring together reading, learning and essential services under one roof. A new multi-storey building will be built on the existing library site. It will include: local registration services; a modern library; a centre for Adult Community Learning (ACL)” New pictures show what Colchester Library will look like when it reopens – Gazette Standard. “New pictures show what Colchester Library could look like after its £450,000 facelift. A project to improve the library began last September when it closed for a year-long revamp.”

Row over library mural as hundreds sign petition – Enfield Dispatch. “Tory councillor says Enfield Town Library mural needs planning permission and is a waste of money when libraries are being closed”

Bridlington North Library to close for major refurbishment – Gazette and Herald. “The closure, which begins on September 1, will see the library undergo a full ground floor refurbishment with £250,000 in taxpayer funding from the Department for Culture, Media and Sport’s Libraries Improvement Fund alongside additional funding allocated by the council.”

Lego fans invited to Barnstaple Library for robotics and coding workshop – North Devon Today. “funded through the Library Improvement Fund” Author Veronica Henry announced as new patron for library charity – Dawlish Today. “Author of more than twenty-five novels, including the much-loved Beach Hut series, Veronica brings a deep personal connection to libraries and a lifelong love of stories.” … “We are absolutely thrilled to welcome Veronica as a patron’, said Alex Kittow, Chief Executive at Libraries Unlimited.”

Local author talks back for a sequel – Marketing Derby. “The festival has once again teamed up with the Society of Authors, Derby Libraries and Derbyshire Library Service to organise a second series of talks by local authors in libraries across the city and county.”

New bags of books added to Darlington libraries to support SEND children – Northern Echo. “Each bag contains five books that explore emotions, offer sensory experiences, or are recommended for neurodivergent children. The bags also include information and links to further support.”

Council Customer Service Centre to move to Central Library – Council. Coventry Holbrooks Library relocating and will have ‘improved facilities’ – Coventry Live. “Holbrooks Library in Coventry will soon be closing for good. It is relocating from Holbrook Lane to Everdon Road. Coventry City Council confirmed to CoventryLive that Holbrooks Library will be based at the Dementia Partnership Hub. It will be closing on Holbrook Lane on August 28.”
Theatre celebrates planting of 1.6 million trees – BBC. ” about 7,500 young people in the county have signed up for the Story Garden-themed Summer Reading Challenge 2025.”

Caerphilly library closures ‘on pause’ after challenge – South Wales Argus. “Plans to close libraries in Caerphilly County Borough are “on pause” pending a “last-minute legal challenge”.” … “A solicitor at the law firm handling the judicial review request has praised campaigners’ “dogged determination” to save “such important community assets”. The council’s leader called news of the challenge “disappointing” and threatened other service areas could face cuts as a consequence.” see also Library closures on hold amid legal challenge – BBC.

Moulsecoomb Library ‘stench’ due to toilet roll shortage – Argus. “As of Tuesday (August 19) there had not been any toilet paper for two days.” … “It is incredibly frustrating as it makes no sense. If the staff at Jubilee Library were denied toilet paper they would stop working.””

entity: Bridgend – Award-winning 21 Book Challenge Returns to Awen Libraries
text: Awen Libraries (media release). “Awen Libraries is set to spark the joy of reading with the return of the award-winning 21 Book Challenge, designed specifically for adults. Over 600 people signed up for the inaugural challenge last year, more than double the numbers anticipated.” … “Using a 21 Book Challenge bingo-style sheet, participants can record their progress and collect prizes including bespoke pens, bookmarks, tote bags and reading lights after completing 7, 14 and 21 books.”

Birmingham’s residents back calls to turn a page on library funding – new study reveals – Birmingham World. “Better Libraries reveals overwhelming public support for greater investment in libraries across the UK, with particularly strong backing in Birmingham. The charity social enterprise found that Birmingham has one of the strongest levels of support for libraries in the UK, with 78% of residents wanting more funding to secure their role in communities.” … ” libraries in Birmingham are delivering real value, from saving users an average of £1,472 a year to helping people find jobs, start side hustles, and combat loneliness. The survey also showed that 1 in 3 Brits (34%) say having a nearby library makes a neighbourhood more appealing, beating traditional favourites like local schools (28%) and coming just behind parks (51%) and low crime (50%).”
Back to school with Barnet libraries – Barnet Post.

Argyll and Bute library closure plan sparks local fury – Herald. Partial paywall. “Controversial plans to close four libraries in Argyll and Bute were pushed through without proper consultation, sparking a furious local backlash and accusations of operating “in the shadows”.” Plan to permanently close four libraries scrapped – BBC. “The sites in Cardross, Tarbert, Tiree and Rosneath were under threat after being omitted from operator Live Argyll’s business plan for 2025 to 2027. But Argyll and Bute Council said it had been advised by the organisation that it no longer planned to shut any libraries.”

Christian Nationalists in this town don’t want people to read certain library books – so they’re stealing them – Americans United. “Leaders of the Reformation Church of Shelbyville say what they’re doing is civil disobedience. In fact, the technical term for it is “stealing” … “They’ve also assailed drag queen events at a local tavern (that has since closed) and tried to shut down a Halloween-themed event sponsored by the local chamber of commerce, where attendees dress as witches to raise money for local charitable causes.” PEN to Put $1.4m Grant Toward Public Libraries – Publishers Weekly. “The Mellon Foundation has awarded PEN America $1.4 million to support its efforts defending the freedom to read. In an announcement August 15, PEN said that the money will be used to support public libraries and librarians, who are “facing escalating threats to their work, safety and core mission.””

Libraries Commission Partners with Riyadh Municipality to Launch Cultural House Initiative – Saudi Press Agency. “The Cultural House is a modern, multi-purpose library designed to serve diverse community needs. Situated within the Riyadh Oases, it features a library, dedicated spaces for adults and children, shared workspaces, a technology lab, a café, and open courtyards for hosting artistic and cultural events.”

History of Chinese libraries, from huge palace collections to public spaces of learning – South China Morning Post. “For the first time in Chinese history, libraries were designed not just as imperial treasuries or a gentleman’s prize collection, but as a public institution. I have greatly benefited from this public institution. I am still an avid reader with a wide and eclectic range of interests, though I frequent bookstores instead of public libraries.”

Can libraries stop AI slop from flooding their shelves? – CBC. “AI slop is everywhere – and now it’s hitting libraries. AI-generated books are slipping into library catalogues and even landing on physical shelves. Some are so polished that even librarians are fooled. We hear from journalist Emanuel Maiberg on how this industry is exploding, and from Laura Winton, Vice-Chair of the Canadian Federation of Library Associations, and Jennie Rose Halperin, executive director of Library Futures, on how this could erode trust in libraries – and what readers need to look for.”

Libraries a secret weapon against ignorance and isolation – Flinders University. “Beyond the Books celebrates the dynamic relationship between the State Library of South Australia – recently ranked the second most “beautiful” library in the world – and its citizens, their identity and way of life. Despite the initial focus on South Australia, it’s a story that will resonate across Australia and its many cultural bodies.”
Chislehurst Library refurbished
Keith Library hours may be cut
New children’s library in Exeter
Customer services moves into Central Library
Threatened closures withdrawn
Are you taking part? – CBBC.
Interesting things about mobile libraries – Artefacto. Five facts, and more, about mobiles.

‘Betty the cat makes a great mascot for the library’ – BBC. “Acomb Explore library has barely been open two hours and already there’s a team member sleeping on the job – and in full view of the customers too. Luckily for Betty the cat, napping is all part of her unofficial job description, as the self-appointed feline mascot. “She comes in pretty much every day – quite often she’ll see me parking up my bike or my car and she’ll come and meet me, waiting to be let in,” manager Fiona Reilly explains.” … “Staff dubbed her ‘The Great Catsby’ before discovering not only did she have a real name, but also a loving family and two feline siblings, living close by.”

Libraries Unlocked Launches Next Week at Tenbury Library – Council. “Libraries Unlocked is a free membership upgrade that allows customers aged 15+ and local community groups to access the library outside staffed hours, from 8am to 8pm, Monday to Saturday.” The Hive: Worcester library features on national podcast – Worcester News. “Professor David Green CBE DL, vice chancellor and chief executive of the University of Worcester, appeared on the Times Higher Education podcast Campus to discuss the city’s distinctive library and learning centre. The episode explored the library’s origins, design, and lasting impact on the community.”

Council library decision paused as ‘disrespectful’ staff don’t turn up – Liverpool Echo. “An important decision concerning the future of Wirral’s libraries has been postponed after a key council officer failed to turn up to a meeting. A leading councillor said it was not good enough, disrespectful, and unacceptable” … “As part of this review, councillors requested information on the condition of each individual library so they can work out how much it is likely to cost keeping them open. However no council officer from the council’s assets department was able to attend the meeting to present the report.”
Wiltshire libraries introduce new apps to make it easier to get books – Salisbury Journal. Libby and Solus.

Barrow Library to Host Creative ‘Our Freedom: Then and Now’ Project Marking 80 Years Since VE/VJ Day – Council. “one of just 20 libraries in the UK awarded funding to create an original local project and host a series of events reflecting on what “freedom” means”. Poet and ” 24 page comic book inspired by Barrow residents’ memories and stories of freedom”.

Celebrating One Year of Community Hubs – With More To Come – Westminster Labour. “Labour-led Westminster City Council is celebrating the first anniversary of its first Community Hubs at Victoria Library and Charing Cross Library. Over the past 12 months, these vibrant spaces have become essential places for face-to-face access to Council services and activities and support provided by community and voluntary sector organisations.”

Warwickshire Libraries bookmark design competition is back for 2025 – Council. “Whether you’re a budding illustrator, a comic artist in the making, or just love to doodle – this is your chance to shine.” Summer Reading Challenge 2025 – Still time to join – Council. “More than 2,500 children have already signed up”

“It’s more than just reading, it’s about bonding, learning, and growing together”: Wakefield’s biggest ever cohort of young readers graduate from Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library – Wakefield Express. “nearly 70,000 books gifted to almost 2,540 children across Wakefield since 2017.”

Sale Library to close for major refurbishment in September – Messenger. “The transformation will turn the library into a ‘state-of-the-art facility’ and include a permanent exhibition space for the Cosgrove Hall Films Archive.”

Swindon libraries to host children’s summer events – This is Wiltshire. Crafts. see also Swindon libraries Summer Reading Challenge launched – This is Wiltshire. “Older children, aged 12 and above, can take part in a Book Bingo Challenge for the chance to win a £30 voucher.”

Plans submitted for huge refurbishment of Ipswich Library – Ipswich Star. ” the public library in Northgate Street could see a raft of changes including a new children’s library, more public toilets and makers spaces found throughout the building …”

Six new community libraries to open across St Helens borough – St Helens Star. “The libraries will be established across the St Helens borough after community groups secured nearly £25,000 in funding through the first round of the Community Libraries Grant Scheme, launched earlier this year by St Helens Borough Council.” … “four of the borough’s libraries – Garswood, Rainhill, Rainford and Parr closed as part of cost-cutting moves and modernisation of the service. Peter Street and Billinge libraries also did not reopen following periods of closure.” .. replaced by “book exchanges, computer and internet access, job search support, CV writing help, community cafes, board games, and youth services.”

More than 8,000 children sign up for Summer Reading Challenge – Council. “This year’s challenge has over 1,000 more young readers picking up books and getting involved than at the same point last year.” School uniform markets return to Staffordshire – Hello Rayo. “The Pre-Loved Uniform Markets, run by Staffordshire County Council’s Libraries and Arts Service and The Salvation Army, will take place between Monday 11 and Friday 15 August at The Salvation Army’s centre in Hednesford.”

Southampton City Council Library service invites local families to discover the joy of reading with the 2025 ‘Story Garden’ Summer Reading Challenge – Council. Southampton libraries transformed into ‘Story Gardens’ – Southern Daily Echo.

MP Anna Sabine joins mobile library across nearby villages – Journal. “MP for Frome and East Somerset joined the Somerset Mobile Library last week as it made its regular stops in Leigh-on-Mendip, Coleford and Stoke St Michael.” Library room named after inspirational Public Health leader – Council. “A room, named in honour of an inspirational member of Somerset Council’s Public Health team, has been opened at Yeovil Library. The Finnis Room is dedicated to the memory of Louise Finnis who led work on Public Mental Health with imagination, creativity and dedication. She sadly died only a few days after she retired”

Restaurant plan for listed library moves forward – BBC. “Carnegie Library, on College Road, Crosby, has been vacant since being closed down by Sefton Council in 2013 as part of a “libraries review” and in an effort to save money. On Thursday, restaurant chain Moose Coffee confirmed it had completed the next step in its bid to take over part of the building” Over 2,000 children enjoy Summer Reading Challenge as they visit libraries across Sefton – Stand Up For Southport. Story Garden. Library staff have made “almost 60 school visits to promote the Challenge”

Community claims council ignored bid for Carnegie library – BBC. “The 125-year-old Carnegie Library in Jedburgh was closed by Scottish Borders Council during the Covid pandemic. Despite talks taking place over a community asset transfer, the B-listed building has been put up for sale on the open market for offers over £140,000. Scottish Borders Council said its officers were continuing to engage with”

Lost library book found in Paris returned to the UK – BBC. “An eagle-eyed Parisienne found it on Metro Line 1 in the French capital a few weeks later and messaged the library to find out how to send it back. Library staff have now contacted the original borrower to reassure them the book has been returned.”

More holiday family fun in Plymouth – Council. Crafts in libraries. “£500 from the Rotary Club in support of their ‘book appeal’ to get children reading this summer … This follows a previous eight-month book buying ban by Peterborough City Council which resulted in shelves depleted of fresh and inspiring novels.” Banking meets books: Local library welcomes Santander – Council. “With Santander closing its Plympton branch this week, the library is stepping in to keep face-to-face banking alive in the heart of the community. Every Wednesday from 10am to 5pm, Santander customers can pop into the library and speak to a Community Banker as part of the new Santander Local service.”

Library praises ‘heart-warming’ donation of books – BBC. “In June, Woodston Library in Peterborough, alongside St Augustine’s Junior School, launched a campaign to tackle the city’s low literacy rates ahead of the Summer Reading Challenge, a national initiative encouraging pupils to read six books during the summer holiday. Jennie Storey from Friends of Woodston Library said they had “books coming in from all over the country.””

‘We’re definitely not shutting any libraries’ says Reform County Council leader – Nottinghamshire Live. “Nottinghamshire’s libraries have been run and operated by the organisation, Inspire, since 2016, with a total of 60 across the county” … “he new Reform leader of the council, Mick Barton, says the new authority is “on the same page” as the previous administration” and wants to make libraries more “streamlined”.

Librarians told not to express views on cuts – BBC. “All libraries run by North Somerset Council are under threat of reduced hours and three have been earmarked for closure. The move comes after the council announced it was axing its annual spending on libraries by £433k.” … “Worle Library, Pill Library and Winscombe Library are all under threat of closure under the plans, although one library in either Pill or Winscombe could be kept open.” Consultation launched over North Somerset libraries – Greatest Hits Radio. “A 12-week consultation launched inviting people who live, work, or study in North Somerset to help shape the future of the library service.”

‘Book bus’ axed due to decline in use – BBC. “The book bus has been visiting Tynemouth twice weekly since the closure of the library in 2020, and it also serves care home and sheltered accommodation residents. North Tyneside Council has now said that it will be scrapped due to low usage and that the vehicle has reached the end of its lifespan.” Forgotten poet of the Troubles back in the spotlight – BBC. “The plaque was unveiled at Falls Road Library for the Belfast-born writer who was celebrated in the US and at home for stark and compassionate poems that focused on the violence of the Troubles.”

Drag artist at library event says she is victim of ‘false accusations online’ – Standard. “A drag artist who took part in a storytelling event for children at a Belfast library which was targeted by protesters said she has been the subject of “abuse and false accusations online”. Lady Portia Di’Monte said the event at Holywood Arches Library on Friday had included a reading from The Chronicles of Narnia and Dear Zoo.” see also Lyons says library drag queen event ‘should not have taken place’ – BBC and DUP minister says drag queen storytelling ‘compromised perception’ of libraries being inclusive – Journal.

Reading challenge where everyone can win prizes – Council. ” Make Your Mark Summer Reading Challenge” … “receive your Make Your Mark card, then collect stamps for joining the library, borrowing books, attending an event or visiting another library” … “The collector’s card has space for 12x stamps and there are goodies such as bubbles, trolley coins, pens, pencils, yoyos, puzzles and more to collect as you take part. There is no limit to the number of cards you can complete. The more books you read, the more likely you are to be one of our Star Readers. If you become a Star Reader you could win a book token at the end of the challenge.”

Library locks its doors when open due to incidents – BBC. “Gorleston Library users must now use their library cards to access the branch on Lowestoft Road “most afternoons and evenings”, after eight incidents were recorded in 2025, Norfolk County Council (NCC) said. Meanwhile, a library in Great Yarmouth has had periods where toilets have been closed owing to antisocial behaviour and vandalism.” New King’s Lynn Library nears completion – Council. “Excitement is building as King’s Lynn’s Library takes shape behind the scenes – set to welcome visitors later this year. Located in the former Argos building, the ambitious project will transform the space and bring together a wide range of services across three floors.”

to-face services – Council. “The service has been successfully trialled at Parklands and Garston libraries since last autumn, and has now been rolled out to Norris Green and Allerton. These libraries now provide face-to-face services throughout their opening hours, with the aim being to roll this service out to all council-run libraries by March 2026.”

The fight to keep two libraries in two of Liverpool’s most deprived areas: ‘It would be a grievous blow’ – Big Issue. “A charity took on two libraries when Liverpool City Council couldn’t afford to keep them open a decade ago. Now a row over funding threatens to leave deprived communities without them” … “The community libraries at Dovecot Multi Activity Centre (MAC) and Breck Road in north Liverpool are operated by Alt Valley Community Trust (AVCT), who stepped in a decade ago to run them when they faced closure because the council couldn’t afford to run them. Liverpool City Council pays £55,000 to fund the libraries every year. Now campaigners say they are facing being defunded over unpaid debts. The council said the trust owes them “substantial debts” over multiple services, including £80,000 on the lease for the Breck Road building.” see also Library closure would be ‘a great loss not only for the community, but for all the people that use it’ – Liverpool Echo. Ambitious strategy for Liverpool’s libraries unveiled – Culture Liverpool. “ a bold and forward-thinking draft strategy that will shape the future of the city’s Library and Information Service over the next five years – and residents are urged to have their say on it. The draft Liverpool Library Strategy 2025-2030 sets out a clear vision to transform libraries into vibrant, inclusive, and digitally connected community hubs that support lifelong learning, wellbeing, and neighbourhood cohesion.”

Summer Reading Challenge fun at Gainsborough Library – Lincolnshire World. “More than 2,000 children across the county have already signed up to take part in the fun challenge at core libraries, which has the theme ‘Story Garden'”

Leeds Council approve plans to relocate Ardsley-Tingley and Calverley libraries to new locations – Yorkshire Evening Post. “The plans will see Ardsley and Tingley Library relocated from Bradford Road to the Tingley Youth and Community Centre on Smithy Lane, while Calverley Library will move to the Mechanics Institute on Thornhill Street. It comes following a four-week public consultation for both sites, generating over 200 responses in total. 64 per cent and 70 per cent of respondents respectively commented expressing their support or understanding of the need to relocate.” Library to close for major refurbishment – BBC. “Leeds City Council said the work at Halton Library on Selby Road followed calls from users to have the centre modernised. The £870,000 scheme will include a new entrance and meeting spaces, improved internet speeds and better access for people with disabilities.”

Over 160 publishing professionals, writers, and illustrators sign a letter condemning cuts to Lambeth’s library service – Brixton Buzz. “It was compiled by local award-winning illustrator Dapo Adeola (Waterstones Children’s Book Prize 2020, Illustrator of the Year, British Book Awards 2022), who has also designed a poster for campaigners (above). Signatories range from well-known local figures to national names such as Adam Mars-Jones, Stella Duffy and Francesca Simon. Lambeth’s annual libraries budget was suddenly cut in February by £1 million (out of a total £4.5m – about the same in cash terms as the 1984 budget, thus reduced two-thirds by inflation). There is no allocation at all for new books in the 2025-26 budget. As the book fund was frozen last November, this means there has been no book fund for nine months.”

Kent Libraries launch Summer Reading Challenge 2025 with fun-filled activities across the county – Council. Story Garden, plus “nature-themed crafts, interactive storytelling, and hands-on workshops.” Update on Folkestone Library – Temporary plans and long-term options – Council. “Because long-term solutions take time to plan and deliver, we’re intending to enhance the current temporary library and bring back a full range of library services to the town centre in a new location. Work on this is well underway, and we’ll be sharing more details with you very soon.”

Discussions on future of family library ongoing – BBC. “The Isle of Man’s Family Library closed its doors on Thursday after directors said it was expected make losses of £100,000 due to rising costs and declining incomes. Signage attached to the exterior of the facility on the Westmoreland Road site in Douglas has now been taken down.”

Romford Central Library opening remembered in pictures – Romford Recorder. “Romford Central Library was opened to the public on July 3, 1965, debuting revolving entrance doors and a separate children’s library.”

entity: Haringey – Haringey libraries delving into South Asian heritage and some summer reading
text: Phoenix. Arts and crafts plus a chance to “map our local South Asian resistance histories in Haringey and beyond”

Blaydon Library to reopen with extended offer for all the family – Council. “Blaydon is the fourth and final library to have been refurbished as part of the council’s Transforming Libraries project, thanks to funding from the UK government’s Shared Prosperity Fund.”

We Make Music Instrument Libraries project, Ewart Library – Great British Life. “hanks to a collaboration between Dumfries Music Collective (DMC), and the Dumfries & Galloway Instrumental Music Service, people from right across the region can now borrow musical instruments, just like borrowing a book.”

HIV and AIDS exhibition on display at Dudley Library – Dudley News. “HIVstory manager, James King, said: “We have teamed up with The London Archives to preserve over 100 interviews that we have recorded over the years.” Punk in Public at Dudley Library – Express and Star. “Led by Mellow Racoon, an independent alternative rock label based in the Black Country, activities will include an instruments workshop, talks, and music by multiple bands.”

‘Sensors’ rolled out at Dorset libraries and toilets – Dorset Echo. “The new technology, already in use at Dorchester Library, tracks movement and usage patterns anonymously at entrances, desks and help counters to show which areas are most used, how long people stay, and where improvements might be needed.” … “The sensors are part of the “Internet of Things” (IoT) and connect to Dorset Council’s LoRaWAN network, a low-power, long-range system designed for connected devices. The council emphasised that privacy is fully protected.”

entity: Lego robots take over Devon’s libraries
text: Exeter City Council. “Libraries Unlimited, with support from Devon County Council, has introduced the hands-on Lego robotics and coding workshops in libraries across Devon and Torbay, funded through the Library Improvement Fund from Arts Council England.”
Spondon Library reopens following refurbishment – Council. “The library has been completely transformed into a modern, comfortable, and energy-efficient hub for the community.”

South London council doubles security at libraries it shut after squatters trashed one – My London News. “Croydon Council has doubled security at its four closed libraries after squatters broke into the Broad Green site earlier this month. The cleanup drew further criticism after books were left strewn across the pavement outside. Mayor Jason Perry has apologised for the “disgraceful scenes” and pledged it “will never happen again”, but residents and campaigners say the damage was entirely avoidable.” … “The council says the break-in happened before staff could remove books and furniture to other branches” see also Library books dumped on pavement ‘unacceptable’ – BBC and Outrage as hundreds of books dumped on south London streets after controversial library closure – Standard and Booked: Mayor Perry deceives over destruction of library stock – Inside Croydon. “while the building had indeed been occupied by squatters after the library closure late last year, in fact it was contractors working for Perry’s dysfunctional council who trashed the library’s stock of books, dumping them in massive piles outside the library when conducting a clearance last week”

Coventry Holbrooks Library relocating and will have ‘improved facilities’ – Coventry Live. ” Holbrooks Library will be based at the Dementia Partnership Hub. It will be closing on Holbrook Lane on August 28.” … “it will now be a dementia-friendly library with improved access and facilities for all.”

Caerphilly council’s expressions of interest in libraries – South Wales Argus. 10 libraries to close on 31 August. “The former Abertridwr, Nelson, and Llanbradach library buildings were made available for transfer, and each received significant interest.” … “The council has expressed delight at the response” to the CAT opportunities. Library users reassured over service cuts – Nation Cymru. “Users of so-called ‘tier two’ libraries in Caerphilly County Borough have been reassured they will not have services cut in favour of larger hubs. The council will make sweeping changes to its library service at the end of August, including the closure of ten sites.”

Newly refurbished Chislehurst Library opening again – Council. “Chislehurst Library will be the fifth library to re-open as part of the £11m initiative to modernise libraries across the borough through repair works and replacement of fixtures and fittings that have reached the end of their useful life. The upgrade work at Chislehurst Library includes a new roof installation, replacement of all windows and a new heating system. will US influence succeed in removing LGBTQ+ books from our libraries? – Boar. [The answer is almost certainly yes – Ed.]. “While it is not occurring on the same scale, the efforts of organisations in the US are undeniably affecting attitudes towards censorship in the UK, with more and more parents requesting the removal of books from school libraries due to the representation of LGBTQ people and stories. Though a common excuse for this is to ‘protect’ young people from being ‘exposed’ to the LGBTQ community, this censorship could be extremely harmful to the very people it claims to shelter. If this removal of content from school libraries continues, thousands of young people, many of whom find themselves at a crucial time in their life in understanding their identity, could be deprived of books and resources that could be instrumental in helping them discover and accept who they are.”

Cost-saving measures to help resolve a shortfall in libraries budget – Edinburgh Reporter. “The changes will see about £345,000 saved per year, helping to make up a £505,000 annual shortfall faced by the city’s library service. Edinburgh’s library service will aim to solve the remaining £160,000 in budget pressure through other interventions. In August 2024, Edinburgh councillors agreed that closures would not be considered to resolve library budget shortages. Across the city, 10 libraries in less socially deprived communities were selected to have two ‘transaction-only’ days per week, where the libraries will not host any events and only carry out day-to-day operations. Officers estimated that this will save about £180,000 per year.”
